title: declarative-config: pin vista deployment image away from :latest (fixes stuck ImagePullBackOff rollout)
description:
Live check against apexalgo-iad (2026-07-20, read-only kubectl) found the vista Deployment (namespace vista) stuck mid-rollout since 2026-06-03 (47 days):

- ReplicaSet vista-5d5f9dc954 has been in ImagePullBackOff for 47 days: "failed to pull and unpack image docker.io/ronaldraygun/vista:latest: pull access denied, repository does not exist or may require authorization"
- The old ReplicaSet vista-7d87bd66df (image ghcr.io/jedarden/vista:1.0.0, 126 days old) is still the one actually serving traffic.
- Both ReplicaSets show desired=1 because the Deployment's rolling update can never complete.

Root cause: jedarden/declarative-config's k8s/apexalgo-iad/vista/deployment.yml pins `image: ronaldraygun/vista:latest`, which violates this workspace's "never use :latest image tags" rule and is currently failing to pull.

Fix: in jedarden/declarative-config, edit k8s/apexalgo-iad/vista/deployment.yml to pin a real, currently-pullable tag (e.g. vista's current VERSION file value, or whatever the last known-good tag on Docker Hub is — confirm it actually exists before committing). Commit + push to declarative-config, let ArgoCD sync. Do NOT kubectl-edit the live Deployment directly.

Related: see ADR-001 in docs/plan.md (this repo) for the caching architecture decision this unblocks. Also related: bf bead for wiring vista-build CI to auto-update this same file so this class of bug can't recur (separate bead, same audit pass).

title: De-duplicate concurrent in-flight badge fetches for the same URL
description:
GET /api/badge in src/server.js does a synchronous fetch-and-score on a cache miss before responding (see the badgeCache lookup around line ~945 and the fallback fetch/score path below it). Because badges are embedded images loaded by many simultaneous viewers of the same README/page, the exact moment the 1-hour TTL entry expires is also the moment a popular badge gets the most concurrent viewers -- and there's currently no de-duplication, so N concurrent requests for the same URL on a cache miss each trigger their own independent live fetch+parse+score of the target site.

Fix: add a small in-flight-request map (e.g. `Map<url, Promise<result>>`) so that when a request for a URL is already being fetched/scored, subsequent concurrent requests for that same URL await and share the same in-flight Promise instead of starting a new fetch. Clear the entry once the Promise settles (success or failure) so it doesn't leak. This is independent of ADR-001 / bf-4pyh -- it protects the origin itself, not just downstream cache hit rate.

title: vista-build CI: auto-bump declarative-config image tag after build, stop pushing :latest
description:

Other templates in that same directory (telegram-claude-bridge-build, news-trader-build per the CLAUDE.md WorkflowTemplate table) already follow the correct pattern: "Docker build + update declarative-config". vista-build does not.

Fix, in declarative-config's vista build template:
1. Add a step after the docker-build step that updates the image tag in k8s/apexalgo-iad/vista/deployment.yml to the just-built version, commits with the standard jedarden git identity, and pushes to declarative-config -- mirror the pattern already used by telegram-claude-bridge-build or news-trader-build in the same repo.
2. Remove the destination line that pushes the "latest" moving tag from the docker-build step so it is no longer produced or relied upon anywhere.

Reference this workspace's CI/CD conventions in CLAUDE.md ("Never use :latest image tags").

title: vista.jedarden.com does not resolve -- add missing DNS record for the public product URL
description:
Confirmed 2026-07-20 via DNS lookup and a fetch attempt: vista.jedarden.com -- the hostname documented throughout README.md (badge embed examples, share links, "Development" section) as VISTA's public product URL -- returns NXDOMAIN. It does not resolve at all, so the product is currently not reachable at its own documented address.

The in-cluster Traefik IngressRoute for this host is correctly configured (apexalgo-iad, namespace vista, IngressRoute named "vista", Host(`vista.jedarden.com`), entryPoint websecure, certResolver letsencrypt) -- this is a DNS gap, not a routing gap.

Compare to the sibling IngressRoute "vista-ingressroute" in the same namespace, which routes vista.ardenone.com and carries external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname and .../target annotations pointing at a Cloudflare tunnel -- that one has working DNS automation. The vista.jedarden.com IngressRoute has no such annotation and no manual record exists either.

jedarden.com's zone is already on Cloudflare (its live subdomains resolve to Cloudflare anycast IPs). Fix: add a DNS record for vista.jedarden.com (Cloudflare, proxied) pointing at whatever origin apexalgo-iad's public-facing Traefik entrypoint uses, matching how the domain's other live subdomains are set up -- or add the equivalent external-dns annotation to the IngressRoute if this cluster's public exposure is automated the same way vista.ardenone.com's is. Verify with `getent hosts vista.jedarden.com` and a live curl afterward.

Blocked on / should land after bf-2n8m and bf-5r6a (no point exposing a pod that can't currently run the right image). Also referenced by ADR-001 in docs/plan.md -- the Cloudflare edge-caching decision has no effect until this hostname is reachable and proxied.
